org.name: Department of Health and Social Care

reports.title: Patricia Green: Prevention of future deaths report
categories: Hospital Death (Clinical Procedures and medical management) related deaths

concerns.quote: Mrs Green had a long wait for an ambulance, despite her age and the recognised risks of being on the floor for a prolonged period of time, due to a shortage of ambulances
The Inquest heard that Mrs [name redacted] wait of 3 hours in ED was not unusual and was due to the volume of patients waiting to be seen and the overall demand on ED

reports.title: Bernard Lyon: Prevention of Future Deaths Report

concerns.quote: The care home in question was recognised as having too few managers for it to be effectively managed but was allowed to continue to operate and was seeking to expand
The home relied on agency staff who the inquest was told struggled to have sufficient grasp of the English language to understand instructions given and to communicate with residents

the Local Authority regularly held MAC meetings to look at care home issues from a multi-agency perspective. The CQC was invited but rarely attended the meetings. As a consequence the flow of information to the CQC was reduced

there was no process to let a family know of concerns that agencies had about a care home or that it was subject to an improvement plan. This meant that families were being left to make decisions about where to place family members unaware of the actual situation and concerns
concerns.hazard: lack of family notification of care home concerns

concerns.quote: significant delays in the handover from the ambulance to the ED team. This was due to pressure on the ED but meant that ambulances were tied up for longer than necessary and then had a knock on impact on the ability of the ambulance service to respond to calls

The Emergency Department at TGH was extremely busy on the day Mr Lyon arrived which was not unusual. The sheer volume of patients who were seriously ill meant that there was a delay in him being given antibiotics in accordance with his need

links.explanation: Both reports describe emergency department overcrowding due to high patient volume leading to delays in providing timely care.
